blocks.title: Faithful are the Wounds of a Friend

texts.NIV84: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring forth.
texts.KJV: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
texts.NKJV:
Do not boast about tomorrow,
For you do not know what a day may bring forth.
texts.DRB: Boast not for to morrow, for thou knowest not what the day to come may bring forth.

texts.NIV84: Let another praise you, and not your own mouth; someone else, and not your own lips.
texts.KJV: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.
texts.NKJV:
Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth;
A stranger, and not your own lips.
texts.DRB: Let another praise thee, and not thy own mouth: a stranger, and not thy own lips.

texts.NIV84: Stone is heavy and sand a burden, but provocation by a fool is heavier than both.
texts.KJV: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool's wrath is heavier than them both.
texts.NKJV:
A stone is heavy and sand is weighty,
But a fool’s wrath is heavier than both of them.
texts.DRB: A stone is heavy, and sand weighty: but the anger of a fool is heavier than them both.

texts.NIV84: Anger is cruel and fury overwhelming, but who can stand before jealousy?
texts.KJV: Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy?
texts.NKJV:
Wrath is cruel and anger a torrent,
But who is able to stand before jealousy?
texts.DRB: Anger hath no mercy, nor fury when it breaketh forth: and who can bear the violence of one provoked?

texts.NIV84: Better is open rebuke than hidden love.
texts.KJV: Open rebuke is better than secret love.
texts.NKJV:
Open rebuke is better
Than love carefully concealed.
texts.DRB: Open rebuke is better than hidden love.

texts.NIV84: Wounds from a friend can be trusted, but an enemy multiplies kisses.
texts.KJV: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.
texts.NKJV:
Faithful are the wounds of a friend,
But the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.
texts.DRB: Better are the wounds of a friend, than the deceitful kisses of an enemy.

texts.NIV84: He who is full loathes honey, but to the hungry even what is bitter tastes sweet.
texts.KJV: The full soul loatheth an honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
texts.NKJV:
A satisfied soul loathes the honeycomb,
But to a hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
texts.DRB: A soul that is full shall tread upon the honeycomb : and a soul that is hungry shall take even bitter for sweet.

texts.NIV84: Like a bird that strays from its nest is a man who strays from his home.
texts.KJV: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so is a man that wandereth from his place.
texts.NKJV:
Like a bird that wanders from its nest
Is a man who wanders from his place.
texts.DRB: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so is a man that leaveth his place.

texts.NIV84: Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart, and the pleasantness of one's friend springs from his earnest counsel.
texts.KJV: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so doth the sweetness of a man's friend by hearty counsel.
texts.NKJV:
Ointment and perfume delight the heart,
And the sweetness of a man’s friend gives delight by hearty counsel.
texts.DRB: Ointment and perfumes rejoice the heart: and the good counsels of a friend are sweet to the soul.

texts.NIV84: Do not forsake your friend and the friend of your father, and do not go to your brother's house when disaster strikes you- better a neighbor nearby than a brother far away.
texts.KJV: Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother's house in the day of thy calamity: for better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.
texts.DRB: Thy own friend, and thy father's friend forsake not: and go not into thy brother's house in the day of thy affliction. Better is a neighbour that is near, than a brother afar off.

texts.NIV84: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart; then I can answer anyone who treats me with contempt.
texts.KJV: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him that reproacheth me.
texts.NKJV:
My son, be wise, and make my heart glad,
That I may answer him who reproaches me.
texts.DRB: Study wisdom, my son, and make my heart joyful, that thou mayst give an answer to him that reproacheth.

texts.NIV84: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and suffer for it.
texts.KJV: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished.
texts.NKJV:
A prudent man foresees evil and hides himself;
The simple pass on and are punished.
texts.DRB: The prudent man seeing evil hideth himself: little ones passing on have suffered losses.

texts.NIV84: Take the garment of one who puts up security for a stranger; hold it in pledge if he does it for a wayward woman.
texts.KJV: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.
texts.NKJV:
Take the garment of him who is surety for a stranger,
And hold it in pledge when he is surety for a seductress.
texts.DRB: Take away his garment that hath been surety for a stranger: and take from him a pledge for strangers.

texts.NIV84: If a man loudly blesses his neighbor early in the morning, it will be taken as a curse.
texts.KJV: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.
texts.NKJV:
He who blesses his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning,
It will be counted a curse to him.
texts.DRB: He that blesseth his neighbour with a loud voice, rising in the night, shall be like to him that curseth.

texts.NIV84: A quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping on a rainy day;
texts.KJV: A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.
texts.NKJV:
A continual dripping on a very rainy day
And a contentious woman are alike;
texts.DRB: Roofs dropping through in a cold day, and a contentious woman are alike.

texts.NIV84: restraining her is like restraining the wind or grasping oil with the hand.
texts.KJV: Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, which bewrayeth itself.
texts.NKJV:
Whoever restrains her restrains the wind,
And grasps oil with his right hand.
texts.DRB: He that retaineth her, is as he that would hold the wind, and shall call in the oil of his right hand.

blocks.title: A Man's Value By What Others Say

texts.NIV84: As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another.
texts.KJV: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
texts.NKJV:
As iron sharpens iron,
So a man sharpens the countenance of his friend.
texts.DRB: Iron sharpeneth iron, so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.

texts.NIV84: He who tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and he who looks after his master will be honored.
texts.KJV: Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured.
texts.NKJV:
Whoever keeps the fig tree will eat its fruit;
So he who waits on his master will be honored.
texts.DRB: He that keepeth the fig tree, shall eat the fruit thereof: and he that is the keeper of his master, shall be glorified.

texts.NIV84: As water reflects a face, so a man's heart reflects the man.
texts.KJV: As in water face answereth to face, so the heart of man to man.
texts.NKJV:
As in water face reflects face,
So a man’s heart reveals the man.
texts.DRB: As the faces of them that look therein, shine in the water, so the hearts of men are laid open to the wise.

texts.NIV84: Death and Destruction are never satisfied, and neither are the eyes of man.
texts.KJV: Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.
texts.NKJV:
Hell and Destruction are never full;
So the eyes of man are never satisfied.
texts.DRB: Hell and destruction are never filled: so the eyes of men are never satisfied.

texts.NIV84: The crucible for silver and the furnace for gold, but man is tested by the praise he receives.
texts.KJV: As the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so is a man to his praise.
texts.NKJV:
The refining pot is for silver and the furnace for gold,
And a man is valued by what others say of him.
texts.DRB: As silver is tried in the fining-pot and gold in the furnace: so a man is tried by the mouth of him that praiseth. The heart of the wicked seeketh after evils, but the righteous heart seeketh after knowledge.

texts.NIV84: Though you grind a fool in a mortar, grinding him like grain with a pestle, you will not remove his folly from him.
texts.KJV: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, yet will not his foolishness depart from him.
texts.NKJV:
Though you grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with crushed grain,
Yet his foolishness will not depart from him.
texts.DRB: Though thou shouldst bray a fool in the mortar, as when a pestle striketh upon sodden barley, his folly would not be taken from him.

texts.NIV84: Be sure you know the condition of your flocks, give careful attention to your herds;
texts.KJV: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.
texts.NKJV:
Be diligent to know the state of your flocks,
And attend to your herds;
texts.DRB: Be diligent to know the countenance of thy cattle, and consider thy own flocks :

texts.NIV84: for riches do not endure forever, and a crown is not secure for all generations.
texts.KJV: For riches are not for ever: and doth the crown endure to every generation?
texts.NKJV:
For riches are not forever,
Nor does a crown endure to all generations.
texts.DRB: For thou shalt not always have power: but a crown shall be given to generation and generation.

texts.NIV84: When the hay is removed and new growth appears and the grass from the hills is gathered in,
texts.KJV: The hay appeareth, and the tender grass sheweth itself, and herbs of the mountains are gathered.
texts.NKJV:
When the hay is removed, and the tender grass shows itself,
And the herbs of the mountains are gathered in,
texts.DRB: The meadows are open, and the green herbs have appeared, and the hay is gathered out of the mountains.

texts.NIV84: the lambs will provide you with clothing, and the goats with the price of a field.
texts.KJV: The lambs are for thy clothing, and the goats are the price of the field.
texts.NKJV:
The lambs will provide your clothing,
And the goats the price of a field;
texts.DRB: Lambs are for thy clothing: and kids for the price of the field.

texts.NIV84: You will have plenty of goats' milk to feed you and your family and to nourish your servant girls.
texts.KJV: And thou shalt have goats' milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and for the maintenance for thy maidens.
texts.NKJV:
You shall have enough goats’ milk for your food,
For the food of your household,
And the nourishment of your maidservants.
texts.DRB: Let the milk of the goats be enough for thy food, and for the necessities of thy house, and for maintenance for thy handmaids.
